title: Greengrid pilot experiment brief and success matrix
content:
Purpose

This brief captures the scope, acceptance criteria, measurement plan, and initial runbook for the Greengrid pilot experiment (internal name: project-sparrow). The goal is to validate that Redwood’s hosted inference pipeline can power Greengrid’s customer-facing outage-summary assistant with sub-200ms 95th percentile token latency at sustained 50 req/s, while preserving customer data isolation and meeting Greengrid’s compliance checklist.

Context and constraints

- Customer: Greengrid Energy (utility provider, regulated PII in incident reports).
- Use case: Conversational assistant that summarizes outage reports and generates concise customer-facing messages.
- Traffic profile for pilot: average 25 req/s, peak 75 req/s (5-minute bursts). Typical request length: 150 tokens prompt + expected 40 tokens response.
- Hard constraints: No raw incident logs leave customer VPC; redact PII fields before any hosted model call unless running under Private deployment (not in scope for this pilot).

Primary success criteria (gates to pass to graduate from pilot)

1) Latency and throughput gate (performance):
   - Core requirement: 95th percentile token latency <= 200ms for the chosen model under sustained 50 req/s workload with real prompts.
   - Measured across 48-hour continuous run with production-like jitter.
   - If this gate fails, evaluate: model variant with lower latency, batching tweaks, or Dedicated assignment.

2) Quality gate (accuracy & fidelity):
   - Automated eval: On a seeded prompt set of 250 incident examples, the generated summaries must achieve >= 85% pass rate on the rubric: (factuality, brevity <= 60 words, actionable next step included when present in source).
   - Human spot check: 20 random summaries reviewed by Greengrid agent triage team with >= 90% approval (no dangerous misinformation).

3) Privacy & data handling gate (compliance):
   - End-to-end proof that PII redaction hook executes in Greengrid’s middleware and that only redacted text reaches Redwood hosted endpoints.
   - Signed runbook and KMS config notes verifying no customer keys are stored in plaintext in our logs.

4) Reliability gate (SLOs):
   - Error rate < 1% (5xx/timeout) over 7 days; automatic fallback must trigger to a smaller-capacity model variant with documented degraded UX if errors exceed 0.5% in any 1-hour window.
   - Observability: per-route traces enabled and surfaced in the console; sampling must include failed requests for postmortem.

Success metrics (KPI tracking during pilot)

- Latency: p50/p95/p99 token latency (ms) and request-to-first-byte (ms).
- Cost: average $/1k tokens and projected monthly cost at steady-state 50 req/s.
- Quality: automated rubric pass % and human approval %.
- Availability: % of requests responded within SLO and % of fallbacks executed.
- Redaction effectiveness: rate of PII detected post-hoc by Greengrid auditors; target false negative rate < 0.5%.

Workshop agenda (Kickoff blitz, 2 hours)

1) 0:00–0:10 Introductions, success definition alignment (Asha)
2) 0:10–0:25 Customer walkthrough of typical incident-to-summary flow (Jordan)
3) 0:25–0:40 Data access & redaction plan: where logs are, transformation points, and sample snippets (Marco + Greengrid infra)
4) 0:40–0:55 Model/latency expectations: baseline models, opt levels, and caching (Lena)
5) 0:55–1:10 Observability and alerts: what to surface in Console, dashboards and SLOs (Samir)
6) 1:10–1:30 Runbook for failover and escalation (Ops + Customer success)
7) 1:30–2:00 Action items, owners, short timeline and immediate blockers

Minimum deliverables for the 4-week pilot

- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): access & NDAs complete; sample dataset (anonymized) available in S3 or shared drive.
- Week 1: Prototype integration (end-to-end) using sample dataset, baseline latency report.
- Week 2: Workshop #2 with Greengrid triage team to tune prompt templates and redaction heuristics.
- Week 3: 48-hour continuous run for performance gate; automated eval run and human spot check conducted.
- Week 4: Final results doc, cost projection, and recommendation (graduate / extend / propose Dedicated).

Integration checklist (technical)

- API keys: scoped key for pilot, rotation policy documented.
- Network: ensure egress rules allow calls to Redwood hosted region us-west-2 (or agreed region); document firewall exceptions.
- Dataflow: redaction middleware deployed upstream; samples of pre/post-redaction logged to customer-only S3 bucket for audit.
- Model: start with rwd-medium-latency-001 (quantized), evaluate rwd-small-fast-002 if latency becomes a blocker.
- Caching: enable prefix caching for common boilerplate language; measure hit rate.
- Rate limiting: set soft quota at 100 req/s and hard quota at 120 req/s for the pilot API key.

Operational runbook (short)

- On-call rotation: Solutions engineer (Marco) + SRE on standby for scheduled 48-hour run. Paging rule: p95 token latency > 250ms sustained 5 minutes OR error rate > 1% triggers incident.
- Escalation ladder: Marco -> Lena (ENG lead) -> Asha (SE director) -> Customer success lead.
- Rollback strategy: switch to cached summaries and a short-status template served from customer side; document user-visible degraded messaging.

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: Unexpected PII in attachments (PDFs) leads to leakage. Mitigation: block attachments in pilot ingest and require manual triage.
- Risk: Latency spikes due to long-range tokens. Mitigation: enforce prompt truncation + streaming partial responses.
- Risk: Model regression on factuality. Mitigation: incorporate a small verifier pass (few-shot check) and human-in-loop for first 500 requests.

Open questions / decisions required from Greengrid

- Is Greengrid comfortable with starting under hosted API with client-side redaction, or do they require Private deployment for the pilot? (decision due by Jan 22)
- Who will approve the human spot-check list and rubric? Recommended approver: Jordan Blake.
- Are there regulatory reviewers who must be included in the audit bucket access? Provide names and access windows.

Immediate action items (next 7 days)

- Asha: finalize pilot success matrix doc and circulate to Greengrid legal and infra (due Jan 16).
- Marco: provision scoped API key and set up rate limits; provide test endpoint to Greengrid dev team (due Jan 17).
- Jordan (customer): provide anonymized sample of 300 incidents and nominate two reviewers for spot-check (due Jan 17).
- Lena: create baseline eval scripts and schedule a 90-minute tuning session (due Jan 18).

Appendix: sample acceptance checklist (to sign at pilot close)

- Performance: p95 token latency <= 200ms across 48-hour run [PASS/FAIL]
- Quality: automated pass >= 85% + human approval >= 90% [PASS/FAIL]
- Privacy: proof of redaction hooks and access logs reviewed [PASS/FAIL]
- Reliability: error rate < 1% and fallback validated [PASS/FAIL]
- Ops: runbook and escalation tested during live run [PASS/FAIL]

Notes to self

Keep prompts small and deterministic where possible. Prioritize observable metrics in Console dashboards so Greengrid can self-serve troubleshooting during the pilot window. If the customer requests Private deployment mid-pilot, run a quick 2-day feasibility spike with infra to map KMS and networking differences and re-evaluate timeline.

Document history

- 2025-01-14 created by Asha Patel
- 2025-01-20 updated with baseline model choices (Lena)
- 2025-02-05 added audit artifacts and adjusted timeline after kickoff
